searchText: quick question.. is there any plan that post-merge where the notion of finality is applied would allow for the eth2 staking contract deposit to be "seen" and applied to the beaconchain in a more predictable and timely manner? this is brought up only as the primary reason for the 2048 block etc.. was to put sufficent delay that a re-org wouldnt impact things.. with finality, this is somewhat redudant.. (in my eyes).. that said, curious what the community's view is on the above.. thx.. Yeah, it's absolutely an intended part of the post-merge cleanup fork to get rid of the eth1data voting mechanism and make depositing more streamlined thank you. unrelated to the above.. RE 1559 implemetation post-merge, to my understanding, each validator will then be responsible for setting his / her own gas limit for each block that is proposed. Today, the miners (decently organized) should put the limit at 30MM for the London hardfork.. to my understanding this is a manual setting overriding the default gas limit.. from my lens, that is fine. as there are fewer participants. however when viewed post-merge and we have a large group of folks that may or may not update the gas limit.. there may be wisdom in updating the default gas limit for the execution cleints to 30MM before the merge.. the concern is that the gas limit will be all over the place. consensus-layer (prev. eth2) call in 1 hour and 35 min from now Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/229 PSA: we are recording the eth2 call, instead of live-streaming. Call may not be uploaded directly, we have different hosts today, we'll figure out the youtube thing yes, we should be able to get the call up in the next few days but no live-stream today! consensus call now! Quick call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/SyZgz4l1Y Apologies that they are sparse towards the end; I had some computer issues. I missed the second half of the call: <@363800010518822915> is increasing prater feasible without flooding and making it useless for new testers? You may as well spin up a new one <@!755590043632140352> do you mean filling the deposit queue? yeah, the needed validators to be safe is a lot it may take years for it to become useful again there is quite a bit of overhead in facilitating a new testnet launch so if we can scatter deposits on prater it is likely simpler to proceed tehre so we need either a consensus change ad_hoc or spin a new one I don't think by scattering deposits we'll get far enough i see, i don't have the numbers handy but yeah if it would be an issue of blocking the queue for that long then a new net sounds attractive 🙂 can't we bump up the entrance rate? that may break clients in unexpected ways fastly changing lists in the state is tough i'd say the fewer constants we can change that deviate from mainnet the better I think the easiest (without starting a new one), is to just allow one huge change with predetermined keys as a hardfork, but that in itself looks terrifying to me, I'm inclined to say that there's no way out of spinning a new one I'm assuming we need about 100K/200K new validators given that we are already at 70% and seeing voting issues in prater so that's 4/8 months of queueing hey devs how we doin today
